My Buddy @Tozetre said it beautifully:

Imagine you wake up one day and you realize you're in prison. Your job, your social life, your personal achievements, they're just posters on the wall of a 10X10 cave, in a pit in a desert. You look out the door to the cave and you see the milling prisoners you're with. You step out and look up. There's rough walls. Climbable, maybe. There's a circle of bright blue sky in the distance. You start remembering that one Batman movie.

Then you look down, and to your surprise you're not at the bottom of the pit. There's a spiral floor that leads down, down, down- but no path that leads up. And below, you can see the prisoners are in worse shape. They're listless, injured, even more light-starved than you are. They have shackles. Even farther down you can barely make out the bottom of the pit. There's movement. Ghostly eyes peering out of the dark, the rattling of chains, and underneath it all a carpet of bones.

Then there's a rumble, and the whole pit moves. Just a little bit. It twists. Everything moves down a couple of inches. You realize that the pit's a screw, that it's moving farther down. You're in a nightmare and it's only going to get worse.

So you grab the wall and start climbing it. It's tough. It's tough as hell, but every time you think about stopping, or even resting, you feel the pit tremble and shift down just a little farther. Soon your hands are bleeding and you're drenched in sweat, but you've climbed a little way. You're on another level. A higher level. It took a lot more effort to reach it going up than going down. You realize that the upper levels of the pit are wider, the upper walls just a little bit easier to climb, but they keep the lower pits from seeing anything above but the steep walls and the distant sky.

You realize you can escape the prison. You can climb out of the pit. It's not easy, but you can get out. You're going to have to leave some of your prison posters behind. You're going to have to leave the free room, the free food it offers. But you can be free. You throw yourself at the next wall and climb it. It's still hard but you know what to expect. You make it to the next level.

You're walking to the next wall and someone stops you. "Hey man," he says. "Why are you climbing these walls?" You look at him in disbelief. You ask him if he hasn't seen the pit below and the sky above. "Sure," he says, "but it's free room and free food here. Why leave?" You ask, aghast, if he didn't see the skeletons at the bottom of the pit. "Eh," he says, "everyone has to die sometime. Besides, I like it here!"

You leave, shaking your head. You climb the next wall, and the next, and the next. Soon you're scrambling up inclines. Eventually you're just walking uphill. There's a lot more people up here. The food is better. The cells are nicer. There's no shackles. Now you're entering a forest, a meadow, freedom. There's mountains in the distance.

And then there's a burbling noise behind you, and a collection of ghouls pours out of the pit. They're grey. They're wearing iron manacles that make their arms bleed. They're wincing in the light. You wonder if they've escaped the pit. But no. They stand and shriek about how great the prison is. They insist that the pit-dwellers aren't worse off than the meadow and forest people.

A young child walks by. The ghouls snatch her up and start dragging her into the pit. You scream at them to stop, but they don't. You scream at someone else to help you stop them, but they just look at you blankly. "Didn't you hear? Living in the pit isn't any worse than living up here," he says. You look around at the grass and flowers. The families playing in sunlight. People smiling. People eating real food instead of the mashed up slop in the pit. You smell the fresh air.

And you throw yourself at those ghouls, kicking and biting and screaming at them to let the girl go, can't you see how much better it is above, leave these people alone, stop spreading your poison.
